LITE.US.name: Lumentum
LITE.US.role: Makes lasers, optical modules and subsystems for data-center links, telecom networks, industrial manufacturing and sensing, including networks behind AI.
LITE.US.note: Proposed step: Lumentum describes itself as delivering lasers, modules and optical subsystems, so neither 'Laser and photodiode chips' nor 'Optical modules and transceivers' fits alone. Source mentions AI (networks behind AI); no CPO mention on this page.

2455.TW.name: Visual Photonics Epitaxy (VPEC)
2455.TW.role: Grows compound-semiconductor epitaxial wafers, the base layers for wireless chips and for lasers and photodiodes used in fiber communications.
2455.TW.note: Site serves HTTP only (HTTPS refused); fetched with curl. Intro text names HBT, PHEMT, PIN diode and solar-cell epi wafers for wireless and optical fiber communications; the English product menu (homeweb_e/index_frame.php) lists PD, APD, F-P LD, DFB LD and VCSEL epi wafers. Page footer copyright 2010. No CPO or AI mention.

3081.TWO.name: LandMark Optoelectronics
3081.TWO.role: Makes gallium-arsenide and indium-phosphide epitaxial wafers, the base material for optical-communication chips, and supplies silicon-photonics components.
3081.TWO.note: Company calls itself a GaAs/InP epi-wafer manufacturer and an epitaxy house; also says it supplies Si-photonics components. 'Data center' appears only as a product-menu label; 'AI & IoT' appears only as homepage banner alt text, so mentions_cpo_or_ai kept false.

3163.TWO.name: Browave
3163.TWO.role: Makes passive optical parts such as wavelength filters, splitters, fiber arrays and cables, and is developing fiber-routing products for co-packaged optics.
3163.TWO.source_title: Browave Corporation 2025 Annual Report (English summary translation), Business Overview and Business Plan for 2026
3163.TWO.note: Business scope: optical communication passive components, modules and subsystems (WDM, branch incl. fiber arrays, AMP, OIN cables/AOC). CPO wording is development/collaboration (fiber distribution boxes for CPO platforms, Optical I/O solutions); the report's product-sales table has no CPO line, so no CPO revenue is implied. Also opened English profile https://www.browave.com/Pages/67.

3363.TWO.name: FOCI Fiber Optic Communications
3363.TWO.role: Designs and makes fiber-optic components and modules, including fiber arrays for silicon-photonics chips, custom transceivers and co-packaged optics systems.
3363.TWO.note: Profile lists 'Co-packaged optics systems' among its total solutions for new product design; no CPO revenue stated. 'FA solutions for SiPh Chip' is from the Passive Optical Products page https://www.foci.com.tw/en-gb/product-category/2. FOCI also has an active optical product line. No AI mention.

4971.TWO.name: IntelliEPI
4971.TWO.role: Grows compound-semiconductor epitaxial wafers by molecular-beam epitaxy for wireless, infrared and optical chips such as lasers, VCSELs and photodiodes.
4971.TWO.note: Optoelectronics category lists APD, lasers, VCSEL, PIN, QWIP, modulators and quantum cascade lasers; says laser wafers serve fiber-optic communications. Also opened https://intelliepi.com/about/. No CPO or AI mention.

4977.TW.name: PCL Technologies
4977.TW.role: Makes optical transceivers plus the optical components and modules inside them for data-communications, telecom, cloud-computing and networking customers.
4977.TW.note: Site serves HTTP only; fetched with curl. Also opened home page http://www.pcltech.com/00-1.htm (engineering and manufacturing services for optical and electro-mechanical components and modules). Site footer is copyright 2013, so the description may be dated; product specs listed there (up to 10G) are old. No CPO or AI mention.

CIEN.US.name: Ciena
CIEN.US.role: Builds high-speed networking systems, interconnects, automation software and services that carry growing bandwidth demand, including for AI-era customers.
CIEN.US.note: AI mention is the phrase about helping customers thrive in the AI era; no CPO mention.

COHR.US.name: Coherent
COHR.US.role: Makes lasers, optical transceivers and related materials for data centers, communications and industry, including transceivers for AI data centers.
COHR.US.source_title: Coherent Corp. Form 10-K for fiscal year ended 2026-06-30, Item 1 Business
COHR.US.note: 10-K says Coherent is vertically integrated (lasers, transceivers, materials) and names CPO among advanced optical technologies supporting AI datacenter architectures; no CPO revenue stated. Filing date not shown in the excerpt read (share count dated 2026-08-10). Also opened https://www.coherent.com/company. ir.coherent.com returned 403.

FN.US.name: Fabrinet
FN.US.role: Contract manufacturer providing optical packaging and precision optical, electronic and electro-mechanical manufacturing for equipment makers, notably optical-communication components.
FN.US.source_title: Fabrinet Form 10-K for fiscal year ended 2026-06-26, Item 1 Business (Overview)
FN.US.note: Item 1 overview does not mention CPO or AI; only the first part of the filing was read. Also opened https://www.fabrinet.com/ (no CPO/AI mention). investor.fabrinet.com returned 403.

2454.TW.name: MediaTek
2454.TW.role: Designs chips for phones, home entertainment, connectivity and IoT, and builds custom ASICs for cloud data centers tailored to AI companies.
2454.TW.source_title: MediaTek ASIC Solutions - Custom, High-Performance Integrated Circuits
2454.TW.note: Proposed step: MediaTek is mainly an own-brand SoC designer that also offers custom ASICs; its ASIC page says data-center ASICs are tailored for AI, hyperscale, data center and networking companies but does not use the term 'AI accelerator', so 'Chip design (custom AI accelerators)' was not used. Consumer-chip part of the role from https://www.mediatek.com/company/discover.

3443.TW.name: Global Unichip (GUC)
3443.TW.role: Provides custom chip (ASIC) design and production services, turning customers' designs into manufactured chips, specializing in AI and HPC chips.
3443.TW.source_title: GUC (Global Unichip Corp.) English home page
3443.TW.note: Self-described 'advanced ASIC leader' with ASIC design service, ASIC production service and IP portfolio; AI/HPC section says it specializes in designing AI and HPC chips. A 2026-01-28 press release title announces a Lightmatter partnership to produce CPO solutions for AI hyperscalers; no CPO revenue stated, so CPO left out of the role.

3661.TW.name: Alchip
3661.TW.role: Provides custom chip (ASIC) design and manufacturing services, including advanced packaging, with AI and high-performance computing among its focused markets.
3661.TW.note: Describes itself as a provider of silicon design and manufacturing services, incl. 2.5D/3DIC and CoWoS/chiplet design and manufacturing management; focused markets include AI and HPC. No CPO mention on this page.
